images.title: Two fish on a scale
images.purpose: Set up the question: a fish of 1/2 kg and a fish of 1/4 kg lie together; how heavy are they together?
images.composition: Two fish side by side at the top with wide space between, and one long bar centred below as a measuring cue.
images.exact_structure: Top left: one big fish filled teal #0072B2 with a weight label. Top right: one small fish filled amber #E69F00 with a weight label. The fish are not placed on the bar. Below, centred: one long horizontal bar for 1 kg, split by 3 grey #6B7280 lines into 4 exactly equal parts, all plain. One question line centred under the bar. Exactly 2 fish, 1 bar, 4 equal parts.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any parts of the bar shaded or covered by the fish, or any total weight written in the frame
images.takeaway: Measure both fish in the same unit, fourths of 1 kg, then count.
images.description: A big fish marked 1/2 kg and a small fish marked 1/4 kg above a plain 1 kg bar split into 4 equal parts, with the question Together: ? kg.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many fourth parts of the bar each fish weighs before adding.

image_decisions.why: A 1 kg bar in fourths beside the two fish cues the common unit while keeping the total hidden.
